Current-main Settings path: The Settings update row likewise delegates directly to the Gateway overlay update action.

## Pre-merge verification

**Scope decision (answers the two open ClawSweeper items).** Landing the Control UI scope. The staged
rollout is accepted deliberately: this is a strict improvement on the default operator path, it adds no
contract the native apps would later have to undo — they can call the same gate — and holding it back
would leave a live one-click hazard in the surface most operators actually use while waiting on two app
releases. #117178 stays open for the Android and iOS graphical surfaces, which this PR states as an
explicit non-goal. No other actionable findings were raised on this PR; there are no review threads.

**Inventory claim re-checked.** `update.run` is still the only disruptive lifecycle action the Control UI
exposes, so nothing was skipped. `ui/src/app/overlays.ts:452` is the sole dispatcher, and all four of its
call sites are now gated: `ui/src/app/app-shell-view.ts:223` (sidebar), `:258` (Settings sidebar), `:452`
(floating card) — all three rendering the one `openclaw-sidebar-update-card` component — plus
`ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts:1010` (Settings → Updates → Update now).

**Baseline reproduced on current `main`, not just the merge base.** At `e9cf5dde561`,
`ui/src/components/sidebar-update-card.ts` still dispatches inside the button's `@click`
(`if (this.nativeUpdateDeclined || !postNativeUpdate()) { this.onUpdate(); }`) and
`ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts:1008` wires `onUpdateNow` straight to `overlays.runUpdate()`.

**Two asymmetries verified as intentional, not gaps.**
- `handleNativeUpdateDeclined` dispatches without re-confirming. `openclaw:native-update-declined` is
  emitted from exactly one place, the eligibility guard in `receiveUpdateMessage`
  (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardWindowController.swift:598`), which runs only in response to a
  `start-update` message the Control UI posted after confirmation. It is the tail of one confirmed click.
- The Settings row pins `viaNativeApp: false` because it has no native-decline listener; a handoff the
  Mac app refused would otherwise end in silence there. Keeping it on the Gateway route guarantees a
  visible outcome.

**Proof.**
- Exact-head CI on `5297e18bf01`: run `31337090561`, conclusion success. Full rollup is 108 checks, all
  SUCCESS or SKIPPED — none failed, none pending. Includes `checks-ui`, `checks-ui-e2e` (4 shards),
  `control-ui-i18n`, `check-prod-types`, `check-lint`, `check-guards`, `build-artifacts`.
- Pre-land structured review of the branch against `origin/main`: clean, no actionable findings.
- No conflict with `main`: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 5297e18bf01` exits clean, so the head
  was deliberately not moved. Behind-`main` alone is not a reason to rebase.
- Landing gates run through the repo-native wrapper: `scripts/pr review-init 121234`,
  `review-checkout-main`, `review-checkout-pr`, `review-artifacts-init`, `review-validate-artifacts`
  (validated), then `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 121234` and `scripts/pr merge-run 121234`.

**Known proof gaps.** No local test execution — heavy proof is routed to hosted CI rather than a local
dependency install. No signed-macOS-app session; the bridge decline path is proven by the mocked bridge in
`ui/src/e2e/update-confirmation.e2e.test.ts` plus direct reading of the Swift handler.

**Follow-up recorded, not fixed here.** Inside the macOS app, Settings → Updates → Update now stays on the
Gateway route while the sidebar card hands off to the app. Unifying it requires moving the native-decline
listener to a shared owner so a refused handoff cannot end in silence. Noted at the call site and in the
PR body.
